report.source_text: On March 11, 2011, the patient witnessed his wife being swept away in front of him by the tsunami resulting from the Great East Japan Earthquake. Following the accident at the FDNPP, he evacuated with his family and returned to his hometown 1 year later. For 2 years after returning to his hometown, he lived with his father and his son’s family while taking care of his father. After living with his son’s family for more than 1 year after placing his father in a nursing home, he began to frequently lose valuable items. He began to suspect that his son had stolen them, and this issue eventually caused the son and his family to move out.

report.source_text: Because the patient’s relationship with his son was strained, we had nurses and support service providers assist the patient with daily tasks (e.g. cooking, cleaning, and taking medicine). Before beginning treatment, the patient spent the entirety of every day outside of the house and was unable to turn off the lights at night. We thought that he might be feeling anxious or nervous and began treating him with sertraline (25 mg daily) in May 20XX+1. Very quickly, he began to spend less time outside, started turning off the lights when going to sleep, and was able to remain calm while speaking about his wife. He would also sometimes spend time at senior care facility and began to look forward to the activities planned there.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 69-year-old male presented with progressive memory impairment and was initially diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease based on HDS-R score of 16 and CT findings of suspected right lateral ventricle dilatation, and was started on donepezil. He had a history of severe trauma including witnessing his wife's death in the March 2011 tsunami, evacuation due to the Fukushima nuclear accident, and subsequent separation from his son's family after falsely accusing his son of theft. At 4-month follow-up, he demonstrated preserved episodic memory with detailed, accurate recall of recent events (emotional fight with son, shopping details, examination contents) confirmed by a care manager, inconsistent with a progressive neurodegenerative process. Blood tests ruled out metabolic causes, and depression was excluded due to normal daily activity and absence of depressive mood. The diagnosis was revised to dissociative amnesia caused by continuing dissociation from the cumulative psychological trauma. Following discharge, he was started on sertraline 25mg daily for anxiety, with rapid improvement in daily functioning and emotional regulation.
